### Describe the bug

With Quarkus 4.0.0.Beta1, a native build of an application that uses both Hibernate ORM and
`quarkus-smallrye-graphql-client` fails at image build time:

```
Error: Class initialization of org.hibernate.type.format.jakartajson.JakartaJsonIntegration failed.
Use the option '--initialize-at-run-time=org.hibernate.type.format.jakartajson.JakartaJsonIntegration'
to explicitly request initialization of this class at run time.
Exception thrown by the class initializer:

java.lang.ClassNotFoundException: org.eclipse.yasson.JsonBindingProvider
      at jakarta.json.bind.spi.JsonbProvider.provider(JsonbProvider.java:94)
      at jakarta.json.bind.JsonbBuilder.create(JsonbBuilder.java:86)
      at org.hibernate.type.format.jakartajson.JsonBJsonFormatMapper.<init>(JsonBJsonFormatMapper.java:30)
      at org.hibernate.type.format.jakartajson.JakartaJsonIntegration.<clinit>(JakartaJsonIntegration.java:17)
```

The same application builds and runs fine on the JVM, and builds fine in native mode on Quarkus 3.35.3.

### Cause

The JSON-B **API** is on the classpath but no JSON-B **implementation** is.

Quarkus 4 moved the GraphQL client to Jackson 3 and dropped its dependency on `quarkus-jsonb` (and so on
Yasson), but the client still brings the JSON-B API transitively through its compat module.
Hibernate's `JakartaJsonIntegration` sees `jakarta.json.bind` and tries to create a `Jsonb`. There is no
provider, so its static initializer throws, and native-image runs that initializer at build time.

Dependency trees for the same application (`mvn dependency:tree -Dincludes='jakarta.json.bind,org.eclipse:yasson'`):

**Quarkus 3.35.3** (works)

```
io.quarkus:quarkus-smallrye-graphql-client:jar:3.35.3
+- io.quarkus:quarkus-jsonb:jar:3.35.3
|  \- org.eclipse:yasson:jar:3.0.4                              <- implementation
\- io.smallrye:smallrye-graphql-client-implementation-vertx:jar:2.18.0
   \- jakarta.json.bind:jakarta.json.bind-api:jar:3.0.1
```

**Quarkus 4.0.0.Beta1** (fails)

```
io.quarkus:quarkus-smallrye-graphql-client:jar:4.0.0.Beta1
\- io.smallrye:smallrye-graphql-client-implementation-vertx:jar:3.0.0.Beta7
   \- io.smallrye:smallrye-graphql-jackson-jsonb-compat:jar:3.0.0.Beta7
      \- jakarta.json.bind:jakarta.json.bind-api:jar:3.0.3      <- API only, no implementation
```

Hibernate ORM is 7.3.2.Final in Quarkus 3.35.3 and 8.0.0.Beta3 in Quarkus 4.0.0.Beta1.

### Excluding the API does not work

Excluding `jakarta.json.bind:jakarta.json.bind-api` from `quarkus-smallrye-graphql-client` fails the native
build in a different way, because the client's compat layer links against the JSON-B annotations:

```
Error: Discovered unresolved type during parsing: jakarta.json.bind.annotation.JsonbCreator.
This error is reported at image build time because class
io.smallrye.graphql.jackson.jsonb.JsonbAnnotationIntrospector is registered for linking at image build time
```

(same for `jakarta.json.bind.annotation.JsonbDateFormat`)

### Workaround

Add the JSON-B implementation, which restores the Quarkus 3 dependency shape:

```xml
<dependency>
  <groupId>io.quarkus</groupId>
  <artifactId>quarkus-jsonb</artifactId>
</dependency>
```

With this, the native build succeeds and the application's integration tests pass against the native executable.

### Possible fixes

I'm not sure which project should own this, so listing the options:

- **Quarkus / SmallRye GraphQL client:** keep `quarkus-jsonb` as a dependency of `quarkus-smallrye-graphql-client`, or
  don't ship the JSON-B API without a provider.
- **Hibernate ORM:** make `JakartaJsonIntegration` tolerate a missing JSON-B provider instead of failing in its
  static initializer.
- **Quarkus Hibernate ORM extension:** don't initialize `JakartaJsonIntegration` at image build time when no
  provider is available.

### Environment

- Quarkus 4.0.0.Beta1 (`io.quarkus.platform:quarkus-bom:4.0.0.Beta1`)
- Mandrel 25.0.4.1 (builder image `quay.io/quarkus/ubi9-quarkus-mandrel-builder-image:jdk-25`, container build)
- Extensions involved: `quarkus-hibernate-orm`, `quarkus-hibernate-orm-panache`, `quarkus-smallrye-graphql-client`

### Reproducer

I hit this in a full application and have not yet reduced it to a minimal project. It needs Hibernate ORM and
`quarkus-smallrye-graphql-client` together, built with `-Dnative`.

With Quarkus 4.0.0.Beta1, a native build of an application that uses both Hibernate ORM and
`quarkus-smallrye-graphql-client` fails at image build time:

```
Error: Class initialization of org.hibernate.type.format.jakartajson.JakartaJsonIntegration failed.
Use the option '--initialize-at-run-time=org.hibernate.type.format.jakartajson.JakartaJsonIntegration'
to explicitly request initialization of this class at run time.
Exception thrown by the class initializer:

java.lang.ClassNotFoundException: org.eclipse.yasson.JsonBindingProvider
      at jakarta.json.bind.spi.JsonbProvider.provider(JsonbProvider.java:94)
      at jakarta.json.bind.JsonbBuilder.create(JsonbBuilder.java:86)
      at org.hibernate.type.format.jakartajson.JsonBJsonFormatMapper.<init>(JsonBJsonFormatMapper.java:30)
      at org.hibernate.type.format.jakartajson.JakartaJsonIntegration.<clinit>(JakartaJsonIntegration.java:17)
```

The same application builds and runs fine on the JVM, and builds fine in native mode on Quarkus 3.35.3.

### Cause

The JSON-B **API** is on the classpath but no JSON-B **implementation** is.

Quarkus 4 moved the GraphQL client to Jackson 3 and dropped its dependency on `quarkus-jsonb` (and so on
Yasson), but the client still brings the JSON-B API transitively through its compat module.
Hibernate's `JakartaJsonIntegration` sees `jakarta.json.bind` and tries to create a `Jsonb`. There is no
provider, so its static initializer throws, and native-image runs that initializer at build time.

Dependency trees for the same application (`mvn dependency:tree -Dincludes='jakarta.json.bind,org.eclipse:yasson'`):

**Quarkus 3.35.3** (works)

```
io.quarkus:quarkus-smallrye-graphql-client:jar:3.35.3
+- io.quarkus:quarkus-jsonb:jar:3.35.3
|  \- org.eclipse:yasson:jar:3.0.4                              <- implementation
\- io.smallrye:smallrye-graphql-client-implementation-vertx:jar:2.18.0
   \- jakarta.json.bind:jakarta.json.bind-api:jar:3.0.1
```

**Quarkus 4.0.0.Beta1** (fails)

```
io.quarkus:quarkus-smallrye-graphql-client:jar:4.0.0.Beta1
\- io.smallrye:smallrye-graphql-client-implementation-vertx:jar:3.0.0.Beta7
   \- io.smallrye:smallrye-graphql-jackson-jsonb-compat:jar:3.0.0.Beta7
      \- jakarta.json.bind:jakarta.json.bind-api:jar:3.0.3      <- API only, no implementation
```

Hibernate ORM is 7.3.2.Final in Quarkus 3.35.3 and 8.0.0.Beta3 in Quarkus 4.0.0.Beta1.

### Excluding the API does not work

Excluding `jakarta.json.bind:jakarta.json.bind-api` from `quarkus-smallrye-graphql-client` fails the native
build in a different way, because the client's compat layer links against the JSON-B annotations:

```
Error: Discovered unresolved type during parsing: jakarta.json.bind.annotation.JsonbCreator.
This error is reported at image build time because class
io.smallrye.graphql.jackson.jsonb.JsonbAnnotationIntrospector is registered for linking at image build time
```

(same for `jakarta.json.bind.annotation.JsonbDateFormat`)

### Workaround

Add the JSON-B implementation, which restores the Quarkus 3 dependency shape:

```xml
<dependency>
  <groupId>io.quarkus</groupId>
  <artifactId>quarkus-jsonb</artifactId>
</dependency>
```

With this, the native build succeeds and the application's integration tests pass against the native executable.

### Possible fixes

I'm not sure which project should own this, so listing the options:

- **Quarkus / SmallRye GraphQL client:** keep `quarkus-jsonb` as a dependency of `quarkus-smallrye-graphql-client`, or
  don't ship the JSON-B API without a provider.
- **Hibernate ORM:** make `JakartaJsonIntegration` tolerate a missing JSON-B provider instead of failing in its
  static initializer.
- **Quarkus Hibernate ORM extension:** don't initialize `JakartaJsonIntegration` at image build time when no
  provider is available.

### Environment

- Quarkus 4.0.0.Beta1 (`io.quarkus.platform:quarkus-bom:4.0.0.Beta1`)
- Mandrel 25.0.4.1 (builder image `quay.io/quarkus/ubi9-quarkus-mandrel-builder-image:jdk-25`, container build)
- Extensions involved: `quarkus-hibernate-orm`, `quarkus-hibernate-orm-panache`, `quarkus-smallrye-graphql-client`

### Reproducer

I hit this in a full application and have not yet reduced it to a minimal project. It needs Hibernate ORM and
`quarkus-smallrye-graphql-client` together, built with `-Dnative`.

In the old recorder-based code, we fired `StartupEvent` based on when all of the recorders associated with build steps which produce `ServiceStartBuildItem` were complete.

In the new service-based code, we're still firing `StartupEvent` after the old recorders which are producing `ServiceStartBuildItem` are done, using `.afterBuildItem(ServiceStartBuildItem.class)`.

Let's revisit this mechanism and see if `ServiceStartBuildItem` is actually necessary anymore. Perhaps we can use a phase barrier for this instead.

Edited to add: The `name` property of the build item appears to be completely unused.

Thoughts & discussion welcome.

### Describe the bug

An application with `quarkus-hibernate-orm` packaged with `quarkus-jlink` fails at startup. The generated synthetic bean for the `SessionFactory` is in package `org.hibernate`, so it is placed in module `org.hibernate.orm.core`, and that module does not link against `io.quarkus.hibernate.orm`, where `PersistenceUnit_ArcAnnotationLiteral` lives.

Generated classes are assigned to modules by their package (#44657).

Fast-jar packaging is unaffected.

### Expected behavior

The application starts.

### Actual behavior

```
ERROR [io.qua.run.Quarkus] Error running Quarkus: java.lang.ExceptionInInitializerError
Caused by: java.lang.RuntimeException: Failed to start quarkus
Caused by: java.lang.NoClassDefFoundError: io/quarkus/hibernate/orm/PersistenceUnit_ArcAnnotationLiteral
Caused by: java.lang.ClassNotFoundException: Class loader for ModuleClassLoader[org.hibernate.orm.core] does not link against package `io.quarkus.hibernate.orm`
	at org.hibernate.orm.core@8.0.0.Beta3/org.hibernate.SessionFactory_Ic7Bcj0-CCy5sfZWPPBFu2wUnfA_Synthetic_Bean.<init>(Unknown Source)
```

### How to Reproduce?

1. Create an application with `quarkus-rest-jackson`, `quarkus-hibernate-orm`, `quarkus-jdbc-h2` and `quarkus-jlink`, with one entity and a resource that lists it.
2. `./mvnw package` on JDK 25 and run `target/jlink-output/image/bin/<launcher>`.

### Output of `uname -a` or `ver`

Linux 7.1.5 x86_64

### Output of `java -version`

OpenJDK 25.0.4

### Quarkus version or git rev

main (d690b790991) with #57426 and #57427 applied; without #57426 no jlink image starts on `main`.

### Build tool (ie. output of `mvnw --version` or `gradlew --version`)

Maven 3.9.x (mvnw)

### Describe the bug

An application with `quarkus-grpc` packaged with `quarkus-jlink` fails at startup. `grpc.health.v1.MutinyHealthGrpc$HealthImplBase` in module `io.quarkus.grpc.stubs` cannot link `io.grpc.BindableService`.

`quarkus-grpc-stubs` has no direct Maven dependency on `grpc-api`; it gets it transitively through `grpc-stub` and `grpc-protobuf`.

Fast-jar packaging is unaffected.

### Expected behavior

The application starts.

### Actual behavior

```
ERROR [io.qua.run.Quarkus] Error running Quarkus: java.lang.ExceptionInInitializerError
Caused by: java.lang.RuntimeException: Failed to start quarkus
Caused by: java.lang.LinkageError: Failed to link class grpc.health.v1.MutinyHealthGrpc$HealthImplBase in ModuleClassLoader[io.quarkus.grpc.stubs]
Caused by: java.lang.NoClassDefFoundError: io/grpc/BindableService
Caused by: java.lang.ClassNotFoundException: Class loader for ModuleClassLoader[io.quarkus.grpc.stubs] does not link against package `io.grpc`
	at io.quarkus.grpc@999-SNAPSHOT/io.quarkus.grpc.runtime.health.GrpcHealthEndpoint_Bean.<init>(Unknown Source)
```

### How to Reproduce?

1. Create an application with `quarkus-grpc`, `quarkus-rest` and `quarkus-jlink`, with one `.proto` service implemented by a `@GrpcService`, a resource that calls it through a `@GrpcClient`, and `quarkus.grpc.server.use-separate-server=false`.
2. `./mvnw package` on JDK 25 and run `target/jlink-output/image/bin/<launcher>`.

### Describe the bug

In an application packaged with `quarkus-jlink`, basic authentication against embedded users rejects valid credentials with 401. Nothing is logged at the default level; with `org.wildfly.security` at DEBUG the only line is `ELY01151: Evidence Verification Failed`.

The password check cannot find the `clear` password implementation. `WildFlyElytronPasswordProvider` is in module `org.wildfly.security.wildfly.elytron.credential`, and the implementation it names, in `org.wildfly.security.password.impl` (`wildfly-elytron-password-impl`), is not linked from that module. Calling `PasswordFactory.getInstance("clear", new WildFlyElytronPasswordProvider())` from a resource in the image shows it:

```
java.security.NoSuchAlgorithmException: class configured for PasswordFactory (provider: WildFlyElytronPasswordProvider) cannot be found.
Caused by: java.lang.ClassNotFoundException: Class loader for ModuleClassLoader[org.wildfly.security.wildfly.elytron.credential] does not link against package `org.wildfly.security.password.impl`
```

Both Elytron jars are automatic modules, and `ModularitySteps` keeps their `.impl` packages private, which is probably the cause.

Fast-jar packaging is unaffected: the same call returns a factory and `alice:alice` is accepted.

### Expected behavior

`curl -u alice:alice localhost:8080/secured` returns 200.

### Actual behavior

401, and with DEBUG logging:

```
DEBUG [io.quarkus.elytron.security.runtime.ElytronPasswordIdentityProvider] (executor-thread-1) Authentication failed: java.lang.SecurityException: ELY01151: Evidence Verification Failed.
```

### How to Reproduce?

1. Create an application with `quarkus-rest`, `quarkus-elytron-security-properties-file` and `quarkus-jlink`, with one `@Authenticated` resource and:
   ```
   quarkus.http.auth.basic=true
   quarkus.security.users.embedded.enabled=true
   quarkus.security.users.embedded.plain-text=true
   quarkus.security.users.embedded.users.alice=alice
   ```
2. `./mvnw package` on JDK 25 and run `target/jlink-output/image/bin/<launcher>`.
3. `curl -i -u alice:alice localhost:8080/secured`.

### Output of `uname -a` or `ver`

Linux 7.1.5 x86_64

### Output of `java -version`

OpenJDK 25.0.4

### Quarkus version or git rev

main (d690b790991) with #57426 and #57427 applied; without #57426 no jlink image starts on `main`.

### Build tool (ie. output of `mvnw --version` or `gradlew --version`)

Maven 3.9.x (mvnw)

### Describe the bug

An application with `quarkus-hibernate-validator` cannot be packaged with `quarkus-jlink`: the `jlink` step fails with `Module java.money not found`.

Hibernate Validator 9.1.3 declares `requires static java.money` (the JSR 354 money API, an optional dependency). `ModularitySteps` collects the JDK modules to pass to `jlink --add-modules` by name prefix: every dependency name starting with `java.`, `jdk.` or `ibm.` is taken as a JDK module, optional ones included. `java.money` matches the prefix but is not a JDK module, so `jlink` cannot find it.

Hibernate Validator's other optional dependencies (`javafx.base`, `org.joda.time`, ...) are not affected because they do not match the prefixes.

Fast-jar packaging is unaffected.

### Expected behavior

The build succeeds and validation works in the image.

### Actual behavior

```
[INFO] [io.quarkus.jlink] Building image with jlink
[INFO] [io.quarkus.jlink.out] Error: Module java.money not found
[INFO] [io.quarkus.jlink.out] java.lang.module.FindException: Module java.money not found
[ERROR] [error]: Build step io.quarkus.jlink.deployment.JLinkSteps#jlink threw an exception: java.lang.reflect.UndeclaredThrowableException
Caused by: io.quarkus.builder.BuildException: Build failure: Build failed during jlink (exit code 1)
```

### How to Reproduce?

1. Create an application with `quarkus-rest`, `quarkus-hibernate-validator` and `quarkus-jlink`, with one resource method taking `@QueryParam("n") @Min(1) int n`.
2. `./mvnw package` on JDK 25.

### Output of `uname -a` or `ver`

Linux 7.1.5 x86_64

### Output of `java -version`

OpenJDK 25.0.4

### Quarkus version or git rev

main (d8126b87f3d) with #57426 applied

### Build tool (ie. output of `mvnw --version` or `gradlew --version`)

Maven 3.9.x (mvnw)

### Additional information

Taking only names found in `ModuleFinder.ofSystem()` instead of the prefix check fixes it locally: with #57426 and #57427 also applied, the image starts and answers 400 for `n=0` and 200 for `n=2`, like the fast-jar.

An application with `quarkus-hibernate-validator` cannot be packaged with `quarkus-jlink`: the `jlink` step fails with `Module java.money not found`.

Hibernate Validator's other optional dependencies (`javafx.base`, `org.joda.time`, ...) are not affected because they do not match the prefixes.

The build succeeds and validation works in the image.

```

2. `./mvnw package` on JDK 25.

Linux 7.1.5 x86_64

OpenJDK 25.0.4

main (d8126b87f3d) with #57426 applied

### Build tool (ie. output of `mvnw --version` or `gradlew --version`)

Maven 3.9.x (mvnw)

Taking only names found in `ModuleFinder.ofSystem()` instead of the prefix check fixes it locally: with #57426 and #57427 also applied, the image starts and answers 400 for `n=0` and 200 for `n=2`, like the fast-jar.

### Describe the bug

A native build that uses the Kafka client extension fails during substitution setup when `kafka-clients` 4.4.0 is on the classpath. The same application starts in JVM mode.

Quarkus still targets `org.apache.kafka.common.utils.AppInfoParser`. Kafka 4.4 moved that class to `org.apache.kafka.common.utils.internals.AppInfoParser` and left no class at the old name ([KAFKA-20297](https://github.com/apache/kafka/pull/22110)).

Both substitutions in [`JMXSubstitutions.java`](https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/blob/3.40.1/extensions/kafka-client/runtime/src/main/java/io/quarkus/kafka/client/runtime/graal/JMXSubstitutions.java) use `@TargetClass(AppInfoParser.class)`. GraalVM resolves that class literal in `AnnotationSubstitutionProcessor.findTargetClass` before either `onlyWith` predicate runs, so the existing 4.2 version split cannot skip the missing class.

The same old name is also hardcoded by the deployment rewrite:

- `KafkaProcessor` transforms `org.apache.kafka.common.utils.AppInfoParser`
- `AppInfoClassVisitor` matches `org/apache/kafka/common/utils/AppInfoParser`
- `SmallRyeReactiveMessagingKafkaProcessor` filters logs from the old class name

The current `main` sources still use the old name. I checked the published jars: 4.3.1 contains only `org/apache/kafka/common/utils/AppInfoParser*.class`; 4.4.0 contains only `org/apache/kafka/common/utils/internals/AppInfoParser*.class`.

### Expected behavior

A native image should build with the Kafka client version that Quarkus can resolve, including `kafka-clients` 4.4.0. JMX removal should follow `AppInfoParser` at its new internal package.

### Actual behavior

Native image generation stops after about 9 seconds, before analysis:

```
java.lang.TypeNotPresentException: Type org.apache.kafka.common.utils.AppInfoParser not present
Caused by: java.lang.ClassNotFoundException: org.apache.kafka.common.utils.AppInfoParser
	at com.oracle.svm.hosted.substitute.AnnotationSubstitutionProcessor.findTargetClass(AnnotationSubstitutionProcessor.java:1061)
```

JVM startup of the same application succeeds.

### How to Reproduce?

Observed while building a Quarkus 3.40.1 application that already uses the Kafka client extension. The only relevant change was forcing `org.apache.kafka:kafka-clients` from 4.3.1 to 4.4.0.

1. Use Quarkus 3.40.1 with `quarkus-kafka-client` (directly or through `quarkus-messaging-kafka`).
2. Override `kafka-clients` to 4.4.0.
3. Run the native build (`mvn package -Dnative`, or the Quarkus container build).

Public run, two independent native jobs, same failure: https://github.com/huahill/jfoundry/actions/runs/38598209157

The Java 25 JVM job in that run passed. The native jobs use `quay.io/quarkus/ubi9-quarkus-mandrel-builder-image:jdk-25` and log `MANDREL 25.0.4.1 JDK 25.0.4.1+1-LTS`. With 4.3.1, those native jobs pass.

### Output of `uname -a` or `ver`

GitHub-hosted Linux runner (`ubuntu-latest`).

### Output of `java -version`

JDK 25 for the JVM tests. Native image runs inside the Mandrel builder above.

### Mandrel or GraalVM version (if different from Java)

Mandrel 25.0.4.1 (`quay.io/quarkus/ubi9-quarkus-mandrel-builder-image:jdk-25`)

### Quarkus version or git rev

3.40.1. The same `JMXSubstitutions` class reference is still present on current `main`.

### Build tool (ie. output of `mvnw --version` or `gradlew --version`)

Maven

### Additional information

`SecurityUtils`, `ConfigUtils`, and `LogContext` moved in the same Kafka change. I did not find Quarkus references to their old names; `AppInfoParser` is the reference that fails the build.

Using `@TargetClass(className = "...")` for both the old and new names, with `onlyWith` based on which class is actually present, would keep older clients working. The string-based bytecode transform and the SmallRye log-filter name need the same new class name, otherwise JMX skipping silently stops matching on 4.4.

### Description

Today Quarkus apps that need a cluster-wide lock either roll their own on top of Redis/a database, or use ShedLock (via quarkus-shedlock), which is built for "run this scheduled job on one node only" and offers no blocking `lock()`, wait timeout, reentrancy or lease renewal. Nothing in Quarkus or Quarkiverse currently offers a plain distributed `java.util.concurrent.locks.Lock`.

Proposed scope:

- **Programmatic API**: `LockRegistry.obtain(key)` returns a `java.util.concurrent.locks.Lock`, plus helpers such as `executeLocked("key", () -> ...)`, `tryExecuteLocked(...)` and a Mutiny `Uni` variant.
- **Annotation**: `@Locked("key")` on a method. Entering the method acquires the lock or waits, and returning or throwing releases it. The wait timeout is set on the annotation or in `application.properties`, and an optional `SKIP` mode gives ShedLock-like behaviour for `@Scheduled` methods.
- **Pluggable providers**: The core ships an in-JVM default, so the API works with zero configuration. Backends are separate extensions selected by config (`quarkus.lock.type=...`), like `quarkus.cache.type`.
- **First distributed provider: NATS JetStream KV**:
  - Acquire is create-if-absent and renewal is a revision CAS.
  - Lease expiry is enforced server-side (bucket max-age), so client clock skew doesn't matter.
  - The KV revision is exposed as a fencing token.
- **Later providers**: Redis and JDBC can follow as separate modules on the same SPI.

Built with the usual Quarkus extension practices: build-time validation of lock keys and timeouts, dev services through the backend extension, and native image support.

A design document is available at https://github.com/Saphri/quarkus-distributed-lock/blob/main/docs/design.md

Interested in this extension, please +1 via the emoji/reaction feature of GitHub (top right).

### Additional context

I'm a contributor to the Quarkiverse Reactive Messaging NATS JetStream extension and maintain a NATS KV backend for the Quarkus cache API (https://github.com/Saphri/quarkus-nats-cache). The NATS lock provider builds on the same extension's client, connection config and dev services, so it fits into the existing NATS support rather than adding a second client. If maintainers prefer, I'm open to placing the NATS provider alongside that extension instead.

Prior art considered:

- **Spring Integration `LockRegistry`**: The API model, with in-JVM, Redis, JDBC and Zookeeper registries.
- **quarkus-shedlock**: Scheduled-job focused. A `LockRegistry`-backed ShedLock `LockProvider` adapter could be offered so both work together.
- **kekingcn/quarkus-redis-klock**: Annotation-only and Redis-only.
- **ShedLock's JetStream provider**: Lease only, based on client clocks, with no renewal.

One of the few legitimate use cases for `onlyIf` on build steps is to gate a step on a configuration switch (almost always one called `enabled()`). This is pretty common in fact; however, you have to write an entire class for each individual case, which is heavy and silly.

It would be nice to have some kind of succinct way to do this; say, something like `onlyIfEnabled = FooBuildTimeConfig.class`. And maybe, for rare cases where the property is not called `enabled`, a second parameter to override the property name on the config interface.

We build JAR archives in a lot of different ways. For reasons that are perhaps obvious, I'd prefer to consolidate on `smallrye-common-io`'s `io.smallrye.common.io.archive.ArchiveBuilder` which appears to be fairly mature at this point, and seems to be pretty performant, and is certainly more usable than at least `JarFileOutputStream` and others as well IMO.

My AI agent has found the following usages of archive creation throughout the codebase:

---

### 1. Core JAR Packaging Framework (`core/deployment/src/main/java/io/quarkus/deployment/pkg/jar/`)

This is the main archive creation subsystem — the primary consolidation target.

| Class                                   | API Used                                                                   | Purpose                                                             |
| --------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ArchiveCreator` (interface)            | —                                                                          | Quarkus's own archive abstraction                                   |
| `ParallelCommonsCompressArchiveCreator` | Apache Commons Compress `ZipArchiveOutputStream`                           | Parallel-capable ZIP/JAR writing; the primary `ArchiveCreator` impl |
| `ZipFileSystemArchiveCreator`           | `FileSystems.newFileSystem` (ZipFS)                                        | Alternative `ArchiveCreator` impl using NIO ZipFileSystem           |
| `AbstractFastJarBuilder`                | uses `ParallelCommonsCompressArchiveCreator`                               | Builds fast-jar format (5 archive creations)                        |
| `AbstractLegacyThinJarBuilder`          | uses `ParallelCommonsCompressArchiveCreator`                               | Builds legacy thin-jar format                                       |
| `UberJarBuilder`                        | uses `ParallelCommonsCompressArchiveCreator` + `FileSystems.newFileSystem` | Builds uber-jar format                                              |

### 2. JAR Unsigning (`core/deployment/.../pkg/JarUnsigner.java`)

- **API:** `java.util.jar.JarOutputStream`
- **Purpose:** Re-creates JARs with signatures stripped. Two separate code paths (lines 58 and 119), both manually writing `JarEntry`/`JarOutputStream`.

### 3. Dev Mode Launcher JAR (`core/deployment/.../dev/DevModeCommandLineBuilder.java`)

- **API:** `java.util.zip.ZipOutputStream`
- **Purpose:** Creates a thin manifest-only JAR for dev-mode classpath (line 434).

### 4. Amazon Lambda Function ZIP (`extensions/amazon-lambda/common-deployment/.../FunctionZipProcessor.java`)

- **API:** Apache Commons Compress `ZipArchiveOutputStream` + `ZipArchiveEntry`
- **Purpose:** Creates AWS Lambda deployment ZIPs (native and JVM). Sets Unix file permissions via Commons Compress. Two archive creation sites (lines 69, 129).

### 5. Project Scaffold Zipping (`independent-projects/tools/devtools-common/.../compress/QuarkusProjectCompress.java`)

- **API:** Apache Commons Compress `ZipArchiveOutputStream` + `UnixStat` + `X5455_ExtendedTimestamp`
- **Purpose:** Creates ZIP archives of generated project scaffolds (e.g., code.quarkus.io downloads). Sets Unix modes and timestamps for reproducibility.

### 6. `ZipUtils` Usage (`io.quarkus.fs.util.ZipUtils` from external `quarkus-fs-util`)

A utility class wrapping `FileSystems.newFileSystem` for ZIP/JAR access, used across ~30 files for both reading and writing archives. Key **write** sites:

| Location                                              | Purpose                                                               |
| ----------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `QuarkusBuildDependencies` (Gradle plugin)            | `ZipUtils.zip()` to archive class directories into JARs               |
| `TestRegistryClientBuilder`                           | `ZipUtils.newZip()` to create test registry extension JARs (3 sites)  |
| `ZipFileSystemArchiveCreator`                         | `ZipUtils.newZip()` as the alternative `ArchiveCreator` backend       |
| `ExtensionDescriptorMojo` / `ExtensionDescriptorTask` | `ZipUtils.newFileSystem()` to modify extension JARs (add descriptors) |

### Summary by API

| API                                                | Production Write Sites                                                                    |
| -------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Apache Commons Compress (`ZipArchiveOutputStream`) | `ParallelCommonsCompressArchiveCreator`, `FunctionZipProcessor`, `QuarkusProjectCompress` |
| `java.util.jar.JarOutputStream`                    | `JarUnsigner` (2 sites)                                                                   |
| `java.util.zip.ZipOutputStream`                    | `DevModeCommandLineBuilder`                                                               |
| NIO `ZipFileSystem` (`FileSystems.newFileSystem`)  | `ZipFileSystemArchiveCreator`, `UberJarBuilder`, via `ZipUtils` (multiple)                |
| `java.util.zip.GZIPOutputStream`                   | `CycloneDxEndpointRecorder`, `SbomNativeImageFeatureStep`, `VertxHttpSender`              |
| `ZipUtils.newZip()` / `ZipUtils.zip()` (wrapper)   | `QuarkusBuildDependencies`, `TestRegistryClientBuilder`, extension descriptor tasks       |

body_text:
### Description

The reactive datasource gives no way to configure the transport-level options on the connect options that Quarkus builds (`PgConnectOptions`, inherited from `NetClientOptions` / `TCPSSLOptions`):

- `tcpKeepAlive`, plus `tcpKeepAliveIdleSeconds` / `tcpKeepAliveIntervalSeconds` / `tcpKeepAliveCount`
- `readIdleTimeout` / `writeIdleTimeout` (and the connection-level `idleTimeout`; this is a separate thing from the pool's `idle-timeout`)

I checked `DataSourceReactiveRuntimeConfig` and `PgPoolRecorder` / `ReactivePoolUtil` in **3.40.1** and **4.0.0.Beta1**. Neither one sets any of these options. `quarkus.datasource.reactive.idle-timeout` maps to `PoolOptions.setIdleTimeout` (how long a connection may sit unused in the pool). It does nothing for a connection that is in use.

### Why it matters

When the database host disappears without closing the TCP connection (host crash, network partition, a firewall or NAT dropping state, a floating IP moving), Vert.x never learns that the connection is dead. Vert.x does not enable keepalive by default, so:

- An in-flight query on that connection never completes, and its lease is never returned to the pool. A few such events and the pool is exhausted, so the whole application stalls.
- A connection running `LISTEN` stops receiving notifications and nothing reports it.

We hit this while building an authorization cache on top of the default reactive PG pool. A read that gets abandoned (for example a caller timeout) must not return its connection to the pool until the protocol state is known. So detecting dead peers is the only thing that eventually gives the lease back. Server-side `statement_timeout` covers the "server is slow" case, but it does nothing when the server cannot be reached.

Some notes from testing (Vert.x 4.5.34, Linux x86_64):

- `readIdleTimeout` is handled by Vert.x's idle handler, independent of the transport. We verified it on NIO, which matters because native images on Quarkus 3 always run with NIO.
- Per-connection keepalive timings (`tcpKeepAliveIdleSeconds` etc.) only take effect with the epoll transport. With NIO, only `SO_KEEPALIVE` is set and the OS defaults apply (about 2 h on Linux).

### Current workaround and its cost

The only hook available today is a custom `PgPoolCreator`. We copy each `PgConnectOptions` from `Input.pgConnectOptionsList()`, set the options above, and build the pool ourselves. The problem is that `Input` only carries static connect options. Once you replace pool creation, you also have to re-implement what `PgPoolRecorder` does internally for `quarkus.datasource.credentials-provider` (fetching fresh credentials for every new connection, round-robin across hosts). It works, but it duplicates Quarkus-internal behaviour and could quietly break if that behaviour changes.

### Proposal

Either of these would remove the need for a custom `PgPoolCreator`:

1. **Config properties** under `quarkus.datasource."name".reactive.*`, applied by `ReactivePoolUtil` / the recorders to the connect options. Possible names (open to whatever fits the existing naming):
   - `tcp-keep-alive` (boolean, default `false`, so current behaviour is kept)
   - `tcp-keep-alive-idle`, `tcp-keep-alive-interval` (Duration), `tcp-keep-alive-count` (int). The docs should say these only apply with the native transport.
   - `socket-read-idle-timeout`, `socket-write-idle-timeout` (Duration). They need a different name from the existing pool `idle-timeout`, so the two are not confused.
2. **A connect-options customizer** (for example a CDI bean `PgConnectOptionsCustomizer` / a generic `SqlConnectOptionsCustomizer`) that Quarkus calls on every connect option it builds, *after* credentials are resolved, while pool creation and credentials-provider rotation stay inside Quarkus.

Option 1 covers the common case with no code. Option 2 also covers less common transport settings. I'm happy to send a PR for whichever one maintainers prefer, against `main` (4.x).

### Implementation ideas

- The settings are generic `NetClientOptions` / `TCPSSLOptions` settings, so they could live in the shared reactive runtime config and apply to PG, MySQL, MSSQL, DB2 and Oracle alike.
- Docs: a short note that `socket-read-idle-timeout` closes **any** connection that receives no bytes for that long, including long-running queries and connections sitting idle in the pool. It has to be set larger than the longest expected query.

{"repository": "quarkusio/quarkus", "task_candidate_id": 22058, "repository_id": 239, "issue_number": 57548, "github_issue_id": 5883320245, "html_url": "https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/issues/57548", "created_at": "2026-10-16T11:24:41+00:00", "author_association": "CONTRIBUTOR", "title": "Reactive datasource: expose TCP keepalive and socket read-idle timeout for the PG (and other reactive) clients", "body_text": "### Description

The reactive datasource gives no way to configure the transport-level options on the connect options that Quarkus builds (`PgConnectOptions`, inherited from `NetClientOptions` / `TCPSSLOptions`):

- `tcpKeepAlive`, plus `tcpKeepAliveIdleSeconds` / `tcpKeepAliveIntervalSeconds` / `tcpKeepAliveCount`
- `readIdleTimeout` / `writeIdleTimeout` (and the connection-level `idleTimeout`; this is a separate thing from the pool's `idle-timeout`)

I checked `DataSourceReactiveRuntimeConfig` and `PgPoolRecorder` / `ReactivePoolUtil` in **3.40.1** and **4.0.0.Beta1**. Neither one sets any of these options. `quarkus.datasource.reactive.idle-timeout` maps to `PoolOptions.setIdleTimeout` (how long a connection may sit unused in the pool). It does nothing for a connection that is in use.

### Why it matters

When the database host disappears without closing the TCP connection (host crash, network partition, a firewall or NAT dropping state, a floating IP moving), Vert.x never learns that the connection is dead. Vert.x does not enable keepalive by default, so:

- An in-flight query on that connection never completes, and its lease is never returned to the pool. A few such events and the pool is exhausted, so the whole application stalls.
- A connection running `LISTEN` stops receiving notifications and nothing reports it.

We hit this while building an authorization cache on top of the default reactive PG pool. A read that gets abandoned (for example a caller timeout) must not return its connection to the pool until the protocol state is known. So detecting dead peers is the only thing that eventually gives the lease back. Server-side `statement_timeout` covers the "server is slow" case, but it does nothing when the server cannot be reached.

Some notes from testing (Vert.x 4.5.34, Linux x86_64):

- `readIdleTimeout` is handled by Vert.x's idle handler, independent of the transport. We verified it on NIO, which matters because native images on Quarkus 3 always run with NIO.
- Per-connection keepalive timings (`tcpKeepAliveIdleSeconds` etc.) only take effect with the epoll transport. With NIO, only `SO_KEEPALIVE` is set and the OS defaults apply (about 2 h on Linux).

### Current workaround and its cost

The only hook available today is a custom `PgPoolCreator`. We copy each `PgConnectOptions` from `Input.pgConnectOptionsList()`, set the options above, and build the pool ourselves. The problem is that `Input` only carries static connect options. Once you replace pool creation, you also have to re-implement what `PgPoolRecorder` does internally for `quarkus.datasource.credentials-provider` (fetching fresh credentials for every new connection, round-robin across hosts). It works, but it duplicates Quarkus-internal behaviour and could quietly break if that behaviour changes.

### Proposal

Either of these would remove the need for a custom `PgPoolCreator`:

1. **Config properties** under `quarkus.datasource."name".reactive.*`, applied by `ReactivePoolUtil` / the recorders to the connect options. Possible names (open to whatever fits the existing naming):
   - `tcp-keep-alive` (boolean, default `false`, so current behaviour is kept)
   - `tcp-keep-alive-idle`, `tcp-keep-alive-interval` (Duration), `tcp-keep-alive-count` (int). The docs should say these only apply with the native transport.
   - `socket-read-idle-timeout`, `socket-write-idle-timeout` (Duration). They need a different name from the existing pool `idle-timeout`, so the two are not confused.
2. **A connect-options customizer** (for example a CDI bean `PgConnectOptionsCustomizer` / a generic `SqlConnectOptionsCustomizer`) that Quarkus calls on every connect option it builds, *after* credentials are resolved, while pool creation and credentials-provider rotation stay inside Quarkus.

Option 1 covers the common case with no code. Option 2 also covers less common transport settings. I'm happy to send a PR for whichever one maintainers prefer, against `main` (4.x).

### Implementation ideas

- The settings are generic `NetClientOptions` / `TCPSSLOptions` settings, so they could live in the shared reactive runtime config and apply to PG, MySQL, MSSQL, DB2 and Oracle alike.
- Docs: a short note that `socket-read-idle-timeout` closes **any** connection that receives no bytes for that long, including long-running queries and connections sitting idle in the pool. It has to be set larger than the longest expected query.

body_text:
### Describe the bug

With `quarkus.http.enable-compression=true` and HTTP/2, a response whose handler has already compressed the body and
set `Content-Encoding: gzip` gets gzip-compressed again. The client strips one layer and gets the inner gzip stream as
the body. Over HTTP/1.1 the same response goes out unchanged.

We ran into this with Vaadin Flow (`vaadin-quarkus-extension` 25.3), which serves its static stylesheets
pre-compressed with `Content-Encoding: gzip`. Over HTTP/2 the browser got 1394 characters of garbage instead of a
5139-byte stylesheet, and the page had no styles. The reproducer has no Vaadin in it. It shows the bug with a servlet
and with a plain Vert.x route, so Undertow is not involved.

This looks like eclipse-vertx/vert.x#5371 ("Misalignment in content encoding between Http1.x and Http2"). It was fixed
in Vert.x 5.0.0 by eclipse-vertx/vert.x#5372 and is not in the 4.x branch. The reproducer fails on 3.40.1
(Vert.x 4.5.34) and passes on 4.0.0.Beta1 (Vert.x 5.1.8). A bare Vert.x 4.5.34 server without Quarkus fails the same
way (`plain-vertx/PlainVertx.java` in the reproducer).

Since 3.40 is the LTS stream and stays on Vert.x 4.5, could the fix be backported to Vert.x 4.5.x and picked up in a
3.40 release, or could Quarkus avoid the second compression on 3.40?

### Expected behavior

The response goes out with one gzip layer over HTTP/2, the same as over HTTP/1.1 (and as on Quarkus 4.0.0.Beta1,
which also keeps the `content-length`).

### Actual behavior

Over HTTP/2 the body is gzip inside gzip, with a single `content-encoding: gzip` and no `content-length`:

```
s5139.css: 5139 bytes
  /s5139.css                   --http2   wire=1263   decoded=5139   ok                     [content-encoding: gzip]
  /s5139.css                   --http1.1 wire=1263   decoded=5139   ok                     [content-encoding: gzip content-length: 1263]
  /servlet/s5139.css           --http2   wire=1263   decoded=5139   ok                     [content-encoding: gzip]
  /servlet/s5139.css           --http1.1 wire=1263   decoded=5139   ok                     [content-encoding: gzip content-length: 1263]
  /precompressed/s5139.css     --http2   wire=1286   decoded=5139   WRONG (2 gzip layers)  [content-encoding: gzip]
  /precompressed/s5139.css     --http1.1 wire=1256   decoded=5139   ok                     [Content-Encoding: gzip Content-Length: 1256]
  /route/s5139.css             --http2   wire=1286   decoded=5139   WRONG (2 gzip layers)  [content-encoding: gzip]
  /route/s5139.css             --http1.1 wire=1256   decoded=5139   ok                     [Content-Encoding: gzip content-length: 1256]
```

In Chromium and WebKit (Playwright 1.64.1), `fetch()` of the two pre-compressed stylesheets returns 1201 characters
over HTTP/2 and 5139 over HTTP/1.1.

### How to Reproduce?

Reproducer: https://github.com/ch-iwi/quarkus-http2-double-gzip (Maven project, see its README.md).

1. `./mvnw package -DskipTests && java -jar target/quarkus-app/quarkus-run.jar`
2. `./fetch.sh`. It requests each path with `curl -k --http2` and `--http1.1` and `Accept-Encoding: gzip`, and counts
   the gzip layers in the body (needs python3).
3. Alternatively, open https://localhost:18443/ in a browser. `index.html` links all four stylesheets.

The relevant handler, in short:

```java
response.setContentType("text/css");
response.setHeader("Content-Encoding", "gzip");
response.setContentLength(gzipped.length);
response.getOutputStream().write(gzipped);
```

with `quarkus.http.enable-compression=true` and TLS (HTTP/2 is on by default).

### Output of `uname -a` or `ver`

Darwin 27.0.0 arm64 (macOS); the original application ran in a Linux container (UBI 9 OpenJDK 25 runtime)

### Output of `java -version`

openjdk version "25.0.4.1" 2026-08-18 LTS (Temurin)

### Quarkus version or git rev

3.40.1 (fails), 4.0.0.Beta1 (passes)

### Build tool (ie. output of `mvnw --version` or `gradlew --version`)

Apache Maven 3.10.0

### Additional information

- Workaround: `quarkus.http.http2=false`. Alternatively `quarkus.http.enable-compression=false`, but then other
  responses are no longer compressed.
- Not the same as #57175 (Range requests through quarkus-undertow). This one also happens with a plain Vert.x route,
  outside Undertow and its `URLResource`.
- curl 8.7.1 (nghttp2 1.69.0), Chromium and WebKit from Playwright 1.64.1.

body_text:
### Describe the bug

Two things in the OIDC code flow together cause a redirect loop between the app and the IdP in a browser that keeps
deleted cookies for a moment. Neither is wrong by itself, but Quarkus could be more robust against both:

1. **Deletion header.** `OidcUtils.removeCookie` deletes `q_session` (and its chunks, `q_session_at`, `q_session_rt`)
   as `Set-Cookie: q_session=; Max-Age=0; Expires=<the current second>; Path=/`. The `Expires` comes from Vert.x
   encoding `Max-Age=0` as "now". Secure and SameSite are only added for `SameSite=None`, so the deletion has neither,
   although the cookie was set with `Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax`.
2. **Empty cookie.** `CodeAuthenticationMechanism.authenticate` only checks `sessionCookieValue != null`, so a request
   with `Cookie: q_session=` (empty) is treated as an established session: `Session cookie is present, starting the
   reauthentication`. A new challenge follows, which deletes the empty cookie again with a new `Expires=<now>`.

Chromium, Firefox and macOS WebKit drop the cookie on `Max-Age=0`. Linux WebKit (here: Playwright's WebKit on
Ubuntu 24.04, which uses libsoup) keeps an empty, non-secure `q_session` until the `Expires` second has passed, and
sends it. If the next sign-in completes within that second, the redirect back from the IdP carries the code and the
empty cookie. Quarkus then ignores the code and starts a new login. The IdP already has a session and redirects back
at once, with a new empty-cookie deletion each time. This repeats about every 10 ms until WebKit stops following
redirects. In our application WebKit reported too many redirects; in the reproducer the page ends on Keycloak's sign-in
form. Our end-to-end tests sign in again right after logging out, so they hit this almost every time; a person is
usually slower than a second.

We'd like to ask for:

1. An empty `q_session` (or empty chunks, `q_session_at`, `q_session_rt`) treated as no session.
2. OIDC cookies deleted with an `Expires` in the past (e.g. `Thu, 01 Jan 1970 00:00:00 GMT`), and with the same
   Secure/SameSite attributes they were set with.

With (2) alone, applied as a workaround in the reproducer, WebKit drops the cookies at once and the loop is gone.

### Expected behavior

A sign-in right after logout completes. A request with an empty `q_session` is handled like a request without one.

### Actual behavior

Playwright, sign in, log out and sign in again at once, 5 times per browser:

```
chromium: 0 of 5 re-sign-ins failed
webkit #1: FAILED (page.waitForSelector: Timeout 10000ms exceeded.); q_session cookies after logout: [q_session_chunk_1= secure=false expires=1792247470,q_session_chunk_2= secure=false expires=1792247470]; 10 app responses, first: 302 /, 302 /, 302 /, 302 /; ...
...
webkit: 4 of 5 re-sign-ins failed
```

The deletion on logout (as seen by Chromium):

```
/logout: q_session_chunk_1=; Max-Age=0; Expires=Sat, 17 Oct 2026 14:31:06 GMT; Path=/
/logout: q_session_chunk_2=; Max-Age=0; Expires=Sat, 17 Oct 2026 14:31:06 GMT; Path=/
```

The OIDC log during the loop, one block per hop, about 10 ms apart:

```
DEBUG [io.quarkus.oidc.runtime.CodeAuthenticationMechanism] Session cookie is present, starting the reauthentication
DEBUG [io.quarkus.oidc.runtime.CodeAuthenticationMechanism] Starting an authentication challenge for tenant Default.
DEBUG [io.quarkus.oidc.runtime.OidcUtils] Remove session cookie names: [q_session_chunk_1, q_session_chunk_2]
DEBUG [io.quarkus.oidc.runtime.CodeAuthenticationMechanism] Code flow redirect to: https://host.docker.internal:18180/realms/quarkus/protocol/openid-connect/auth?...
```

Without a browser, an empty cookie gets a challenge and the same deletion again:

```
$ curl -sk -D - -o /dev/null -H 'Cookie: q_session=' https://localhost:18443/
HTTP/2 302
location: https://host.docker.internal:18180/realms/quarkus/protocol/openid-connect/auth?response_type=code&client_id=quarkus-app&...
set-cookie: q_auth_8dfdf56e-...=...; Max-Age=300; Expires=Sat, 17 Oct 2026 14:24:24 GMT; Path=/; Secure; HTTPOnly; SameSite=Lax
set-cookie: q_session=; Max-Age=0; Expires=Sat, 17 Oct 2026 14:19:24 GMT; Path=/
```

### How to Reproduce?

Reproducer: https://github.com/ch-iwi/quarkus-oidc-empty-session-cookie (Maven project, see its README.md). Needs Docker for
Keycloak and for Playwright's Linux image; macOS WebKit does not show the behaviour.

1. `keycloak/run.sh` starts Keycloak 26.8.1 over HTTPS on port 18180 with the realm `quarkus` (user `alice`/`alice`).
2. `./mvnw package -DskipTests && java -jar target/quarkus-app/quarkus-run.jar` starts the app on
   https://localhost:18443 with OIDC DEBUG logging.
3. `./run-browsers.sh` runs `relogin.mjs` in `mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.64.1-noble`: sign in, log out, sign in
   again at once, in Chromium and WebKit.
4. Optional: `java -Drepro.workaround=true -jar target/quarkus-app/quarkus-run.jar` turns on the workaround below, and
   step 3 passes in WebKit.

### Output of `uname -a` or `ver`

Darwin 27.0.0 arm64 (app and Keycloak); browsers in Docker, Ubuntu 24.04 (Playwright image, libsoup 3.4.4)

### Output of `java -version`

openjdk version "25.0.4.1" 2026-08-18 LTS (Temurin)

### Quarkus version or git rev

3.40.1; 4.0.0.Beta1 behaves the same

### Build tool (ie. output of `mvnw --version` or `gradlew --version`)

Apache Maven 3.10.0

### Additional information

- Workaround: a router route at `RouteConstants.ROUTE_ORDER_HEADERS` that, in a headers-end handler, takes the `q_*`
  deletions out of the response's cookie jar and writes them again with `Expires=Thu, 01 Jan 1970 00:00:00 GMT`
  (`ExpireDeletionsInThePast` in the reproducer). It has to be a router route because the authentication sends its
  redirect before any filter runs.
- Adding `Secure` to the deletion alone did not make WebKit drop the cookie; the `Expires` in the past did.
- Related, in Vert.x Web: vert-x3/vertx-web#1890 and vert-x3/vertx-web#1956 (closed): expired or removed cookies lost
  SameSite/Secure.
- Keycloak 26.8.1, Playwright 1.64.1 (WebKit build 2370).

### Description

The WebAuthn extension registers its endpoints under a fixed `webauthn/` path in the non-application root:

- `GET /q/webauthn/login-options-challenge` and `/q/webauthn/register-options-challenge`
- `POST /q/webauthn/login` and `/q/webauthn/register` (when enabled)
- `GET /q/webauthn/webauthn.js` and `/q/webauthn/logout`

Only the `/q/` part can be changed, through `quarkus.http.non-application-root-path`; the `webauthn/` segment is hard-coded in `WebAuthnRecorder`, which has a `// FIXME: paths configurable` comment. An application cannot move these endpoints, for example to group them with its own authentication endpoints, or to keep them out of `/q/` without moving every other non-application endpoint.

### Implementation ideas

Add `quarkus.webauthn.root-path` with the default value `webauthn`, resolved against the non-application root path like `quarkus.smallrye-health.root-path`, and use it in `WebAuthnRecorder`.

`webauthn.js` is a static file whose endpoint defaults are hard-coded (`"/q/webauthn/register-options-challenge"` and so on, overridable through the `WebAuthn` constructor options), so they are already wrong when `quarkus.http.non-application-root-path` is changed. Serving the script with defaults computed from the configured paths would fix both. The guide's examples hard-code `/q/webauthn/` too.

### Description

When `quarkus.webauthn.attestation` is not `none`, `WebAuthnSecurity.makeWebAuthn` looks up a TLS registry configuration named `webauthn` and uses its trust store as the attestation trust anchors. If there is none, it builds a trust store from the built-in Android, Apple and FIDO roots.

```java
// FIXME: make config name configurable?
Optional<TlsConfiguration> webauthnTlsConfiguration = certificates.get("webauthn");
```

The name is fixed, and neither `security-webauthn.adoc` nor the config reference mention it. The only way to supply your own attestation roots (for example, a private CA for enterprise authenticators) is to know about `quarkus.tls.webauthn.trust-store.*`.

### Implementation ideas

- Add `quarkus.webauthn.tls-configuration-name` (an `Optional<String>`, like `quarkus.mailer.tls-configuration-name` and the OIDC `tls.tls-configuration-name`), keeping `webauthn` as the fallback so existing setups work.
- Document the attestation trust store in the WebAuthn guide, either way.

Which is preferred: docs only, or docs plus the config property?

body_text:
### Describe the bug

Hello,

This documentation section describes how generate gRPC classes from .proto files distributed in a dependency: https://quarkus.io/guides/grpc-generation-reference/#scan-for-proto.

However, it is not possible to generate them out of the box when using `quarkus:dev` goal. 
The reason seems to be that `quarkus:dev` executes `quarkus:generate-code` before `resources:resources`.

Configurations like these on the application.properties
```
quarkus.generate-code.grpc.scan-for-proto=<groupId>:<artifactId>
quarkus.generate-code.grpc.scan-for-proto-include."<groupId>:<artifactId>"=foo/**,bar/**,banana/a-proto.proto
quarkus.generate-code.grpc.scan-for-proto-exclude."<groupId>:<artifactId>"=foo/private/**,bar/another-proto.proto
```
Are ignored by `quarkus:generate-code` when using `quarkus:dev`.

I workaround this with any of these options:
1. Placing the maven properties into the `.mvn/maven.config` file:
```
-Dquarkus.generate-code.grpc.scan-for-proto=<groupId>:<artifactId> -Dquarkus.generate-code.grpc.scan-for-proto-include."<groupId>:<artifactId>"=foo/**,bar/**,banana/a-proto.proto
```
2. execute `mvn clean compile quarkus:dev` instead of `mvn quarkus:dev`

### Expected behavior

I would expect to see under target folder the generated classes from the  .proto files as specified in the application.properties

### Actual behavior

Executing `mvn clean quarkus:dev` the expected gRPC generated files are not generated at all.

### How to Reproduce?

1. Unzip the reproducer 

[demo.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33689806/demo.zip)

2. Build grpc-contracts project with `mvn clean install`
3. Build the app project with `mvn clean quarkus:dev`
4. See how resources goal is executed after generate code:
```
[INFO] --- quarkus:3.40.1.1:dev (default-cli) @ app ---
[INFO] Invoking quarkus:3.40.1.1:generate-code (default-generate-code) @ app
[INFO] Invoking resources:3.3.1:resources (default-resources) @ app
[INFO] Copying 1 resource from src/main/resources to target/classes
[INFO] Invoking compiler:3.15.0:compile (default-compile) @ app
....
```
6. Check that there are no grpc generated classes `ls ./app/target/generated-sources/grpc`
7. Build the app project with `mvn clean compile quarkus:dev`
8. Check that now there are classes under  `ls ./app/target/generated-sources/grpc`
 
In addition, when the quarkus application is launched, the following WARNs are logged:

```
WARN  [io.quarkus.config] (Quarkus Main Thread) Unrecognized configuration key "quarkus.generate-code.grpc.scan-for-proto-include."org.demo:grpc-contracts"" was provided; it will be ignored; verify that the dependency extension for this configuration is set or that you did not make a typo                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                                                                                
WARN  [io.quarkus.config] (Quarkus Main Thread) Unrecognized configuration key "quarkus.generate-code.grpc.scan-for-proto-exclude."org.demo:grpc-contracts"" was provided; it will be ignored; verify that the dependency extension for this configuration is set or that you did not make a typo
```

Which are harmless, but could drive to confusion

Hello,

This documentation section describes how generate gRPC classes from .proto files distributed in a dependency: https://quarkus.io/guides/grpc-generation-reference/#scan-for-proto.

However, it is not possible to generate them out of the box when using `quarkus:dev` goal. 
The reason seems to be that `quarkus:dev` executes `quarkus:generate-code` before `resources:resources`.

Configurations like these on the application.properties
```
quarkus.generate-code.grpc.scan-for-proto=<groupId>:<artifactId>
quarkus.generate-code.grpc.scan-for-proto-include."<groupId>:<artifactId>"=foo/**,bar/**,banana/a-proto.proto
quarkus.generate-code.grpc.scan-for-proto-exclude."<groupId>:<artifactId>"=foo/private/**,bar/another-proto.proto
```
Are ignored by `quarkus:generate-code` when using `quarkus:dev`.

I workaround this with any of these options:
1. Placing the maven properties into the `.mvn/maven.config` file:
```
-Dquarkus.generate-code.grpc.scan-for-proto=<groupId>:<artifactId> -Dquarkus.generate-code.grpc.scan-for-proto-include."<groupId>:<artifactId>"=foo/**,bar/**,banana/a-proto.proto
```
2. execute `mvn clean compile quarkus:dev` instead of `mvn quarkus:dev`

### Expected behavior

I would expect to see under target folder the generated classes from the  .proto files as specified in the application.properties

### Actual behavior

Executing `mvn clean quarkus:dev` the expected gRPC generated files are not generated at all.

### How to Reproduce?

1. Unzip the reproducer 

[demo.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33689806/demo.zip)

2. Build grpc-contracts project with `mvn clean install`
3. Build the app project with `mvn clean quarkus:dev`
4. See how resources goal is executed after generate code:
```
[INFO] --- quarkus:3.40.1.1:dev (default-cli) @ app ---
[INFO] Invoking quarkus:3.40.1.1:generate-code (default-generate-code) @ app
[INFO] Invoking resources:3.3.1:resources (default-resources) @ app
[INFO] Copying 1 resource from src/main/resources to target/classes
[INFO] Invoking compiler:3.15.0:compile (default-compile) @ app
....
```
6. Check that there are no grpc generated classes `ls ./app/target/generated-sources/grpc`
7. Build the app project with `mvn clean compile quarkus:dev`
8. Check that now there are classes under  `ls ./app/target/generated-sources/grpc`
 
In addition, when the quarkus application is launched, the following WARNs are logged:

```
WARN  [io.quarkus.config] (Quarkus Main Thread) Unrecognized configuration key "quarkus.generate-code.grpc.scan-for-proto-include."org.demo:grpc-contracts"" was provided; it will be ignored; verify that the dependency extension for this configuration is set or that you did not make a typo                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     
                                                                                                                                                                                
WARN  [io.quarkus.config] (Quarkus Main Thread) Unrecognized configuration key "quarkus.generate-code.grpc.scan-for-proto-exclude."org.demo:grpc-contracts"" was provided; it will be ignored; verify that the dependency extension for this configuration is set or that you did not make a typo
```

Which are harmless, but could drive to confusion
